subject: Solace Health MAP: evaluation runway and reservation sizing questions
messages:
From: Lara Dunn <lara.dunn@solacehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solacehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: MAP request + lead times for Dedicated H100 pool sizing

Priya —

Thanks for the demo last week. Solace is keen to formalize a mutual action plan so we can align evaluation milestones with procurement and make a reservation decision for Dedicated/Private capacity. High-level asks from our side:

- A MAP that calls out evaluation gates (kickoff, pilot acceptance, performance regressions) and the minimal acceptance criteria.
- Target GPU pool sizing guidance (we're leaning toward H100s) and assumptions: expected token/sec, concurrency, typical seq length.
- Procurement lead times and what Redwood needs from us to start a reserved pool.

We'd like a draft MAP by next Monday and to aim for a procurement decision by mid-September if the pilot results look good. Attached is our RFP_requirements.pdf and a short procurement timeline from our finance team.

Can you confirm Redwood's typical lead time for H100 pool activation (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private) and any blockers we should surface early? Also, please include the SOC2/controls evidence that procurement will request.

Best,
Lara Dunn
VP Product, Solace Health
lara.dunn@solacehealth.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: RFP_requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lara Dunn <lara.dunn@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + lead times for Dedicated H100 pool sizing

Lara —

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFP. I've sketched a draft MAP and a sizing worksheet (attached) to surface the assumptions we'll use. High level answers up front:

- Typical H100 dedicated pool lead time (contract signed + payment): 6–10 weeks for reserved capacity in our hosted region; Private/VPC on-prem timelines vary (8–14 weeks) depending on networking/approval windows.
- We recommend a staged pool: 4 H100s for pilot, scale to 8–16 based on throughput and batch strategy. If you prefer a phased tranche approach we can add buffer tranches in the MAP.
- Procurement will ask for SOC 2 Type II summary, encryption/KMS posture, and network architecture — I've added a short SOC2 evidence ask doc to the attachments.

Request from your side to finalize the sizing:
- Expected 95th pct latency target and p99 goal (ms) for inference calls
- Peak concurrent requests and expected QPS for the pilot window (2–4 weeks)
- Typical sequence length and average tokens per call

I've attached: 20260815-solace-map-draft.pdf and gpu-sizing-worksheet.xlsx. The draft MAP includes milestones, owners, and dates based on a Sep 15 procurement target. If procurement needs a longer timebox we can shift dates.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call this week to confirm workload assumptions (30 min)
2) We refine the MAP and post milestones to the HubSpot deal
3) Pilot kickoff within 1 week of finalized MAP

Would Thu 8/20 10:00–10:30 PT work for a assumptions call?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Attachments: 20260815-solace-map-draft.pdf, gpu-sizing-worksheet.xlsx, soc2-evidence-ask.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Lara Dunn <lara.dunn@solacehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + lead times for Dedicated H100 pool sizing

Quick technical note:

- For a pilot with 4 H100s we recommend planning for 1–2x concurrency headroom beyond expected 95th pct QPS when using dynamic batching. That usually translates to ~20–30% extra GPU memory budget for KV cache and batching buffers.
- If your workload has many short, latency-sensitive calls (avg seq < 128 tokens) we should optimize for low-latency kernels and smaller batch sizes; that will lower effective throughput and push towards larger pool sizing earlier.
- We'll include a fallback plan in the MAP: smaller/quantized model variants that give cost savings during steady state.

I can join the assumptions call if helpful and walk through the sizing sheet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Infra Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Lara Dunn <lara.dunn@solacehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <a.cho@solacehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@solacehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP request + lead times for Dedicated H100 pool sizing

Priya/Ben —

Thanks for the draft and the notes. Answers to your sizing questions below:
- Latency targets: 95th <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms for synchronous inference requests.
- Pilot QPS: expected steady 40 qps with 95th bursts to 120 qps during simulated traffic.
- Typical sequence: avg 220 tokens / call (we have longer summaries sometimes up to 1024 in non-production).

Procurement notes:
- Procurement prefers a 6–8 week activation window in contractual terms; they will accept a 10-week physical lead as long as we have a binding reservation commitment and an activation SLT. Their PO template attached.
- Budget: target capex/commit consistent with a 12-month reserved agreement; we can share an internal budget band after you send a formal price worksheet.

We can do Thu 8/20 10:00 PT for the assumptions call. Please send calendar invite.

Lara

Attachment: Solace_PO_Template.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lara Dunn <lara.dunn@solacehealth.com>, Aaron Cho <a.cho@solacehealth.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Solace Health MAP & evaluation runway — consolidated plan and next steps

Lara/Aaron —

Thanks for the quick turn on requirements and for confirming the call. Per our conversation on Thu 8/20, attached is the consolidated MAP that maps evaluation gates to procurement milestones and lead times. Key milestones we put into the plan:

- Evaluation kickoff (data access + test vectors): 2026-08-24 (owner: Solace / L. Dunn)
- Pilot window: 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-14 (owner: Redwood / Ben Carter)
- Pilot acceptance (performance + stability): target 2026-09-16; acceptance criteria included in the attached MAP document
- Procurement sign & reservation commitment: target 2026-09-22 (Procurement / Solace) — this date assumes a 6-week activation window to delivery of dedicated pool resources
- Reserved pool activation start: estimated 2026-11-03 (Redwood infra handoff) — 6 weeks after PO acceptance; if you require Private on-prem deployment we'll add the extra networking window (8–14 weeks) in the MAP

We also included contingency lane A (staggered tranches: pilot -> +4 H100 -> +8 H100) and contingency lane B (fallback to quantized variant to reduce steady-state spend). The MAP lists owners for each task, artifacts needed (signed PO, SOC2 evidence packet, network allowlist), and acceptance tests (latency/QPS matrix and regression tolerance).

Attachments included: 20260815-solace-map-draft.pdf (updated), gpu-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (final), soc2-evidence-ask.docx. I've posted the milestones to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/98765.

Next ask from Solace: 1) confirm pilot dataset and test vectors by 8/24, 2) procurement to share redlines to the PO template by 9/1. If both items close on time, the procurement target of ~9/22 is feasible.

I'll draft a short one-page mutual action plan that can be used as an internal handoff doc for your procurement team and attach it to the deal. Please confirm if the dates below look realistic from your side and I'll move the MAP to 'Committed' in HubSpot.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
